ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be conducted against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Hong Kong Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau sanctions list, and the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions announcements. All ultimate beneficial owners, directors, signatories, franchise master licensees, and material counterparties must be screened for politically exposed persons (PEPs), adverse media, and legitimate-source-of-wealth indicators. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP from an FATF high-risk jurisdiction and for any transaction involving a sanctioned entity. Results must be documented in an AML risk assessment form and refreshed every 90 days or upon any beneficial ownership change. A qualified AML officer must issue a clearance memo prior to incorporation and bank account opening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry One-Stop Company Registration and Business Registration Service through the Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under sections 100 and 101 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), an English name is mandatory and a Chinese name is optional. The Chinese name must be composed of Traditional Chinese characters only, and it must be a direct translation or phonetic transliteration of the English name. No Pinyin romanization is accepted as a Chinese name; the English name must be in roman script. Where a mainland-style name is desired for the joint venture brand, the four-tier naming convention (administrative region, distinctive trade name, industry descriptor, and legal form) must be strictly observed. The transliteration of the brand 'Chuan Ma La Tang' must be registered as a Hong Kong trade mark and mirrored in the company's Chinese name to avoid conflicts with existing food franchise registrations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the e-Registry portal issues a rejection code identifying the specific statutory prohibition. The applicant may file a fresh name application immediately or lodge a written appeal with the Companies Registry Name Review Board within 14 days under section 103 of the Companies Ordinance. The appeal must state the grounds on which the proposed name complies with the registration requirements and should be supported by a Hong Kong barrister's opinion on registrability. The Registry must issue its decision within 15 business days; a further appeal lies with the Administrative Appeals Board. Legal costs for the appeal are typically between USD 1,500 and USD 3,200, exclusive of government fees.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox may satisfy the Companies Ordinance registered-office requirement only if a physical street address in Hong Kong is provided and a licensed registered agent accepts service of process. However, for the fast-casual food franchise industry, the Inland Revenue Department and licensed banks will generally reject such an arrangement as evidence of actual commercial substance. The entity will receive royalty wire transfers and must maintain local payroll, a lease, utility bills, and operational management. A virtual office without a Hong Kong-managed commercial presence would fail the economic substance test under the Inland Revenue Ordinance and may trigger a higher AML risk rating. Accordingly, a serviced co-working office with a dedicated meeting room and a physical signboard is the minimum acceptable structure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (a) registered office signboard conspicuously displayed; (b) current lease or tenancy agreement in the company's name; (c) local employee payroll and Mandatory Provident Fund contribution records; (d) point-of-sale terminals and sales invoices from the actual restaurant; (e) inventory storage and supply-chain purchase contracts; (f) active local telephone and internet service contracts. Quantified risk: unannounced physical inspections by the Companies Registry, Inland Revenue Department, and Food and Environmental Hygiene Department are assessed at 25% within the first 12 months and 45% after 18 months if the company records a high volume of royalty wires without commensurate local operating activity. Food business premises are inspected at least annually under the Food Business Regulation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - ss. 5, 67, 100, 112, 113, 231, 474-475; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) s. 6; Food Business Regulation (Cap. 132X); Fire Services Ordinance (Cap. 95); Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499); Water Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 358).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Operations Branch (Incorporation Section), operating the One-Stop Company Registration and Business Registration e-Service jointly with the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NNC1 (Incorporation Form - Private Company Limited by Shares), together with the adopted Articles of Association, the Statement of Capital, and the company name certificate search record, filed online through the Companies Registry e-Registry portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - The Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) imposes no minimum paid-up capital requirement and no blocked escrow/paid-in capital account for a private company limited by shares; the subscriber shares need not be fully paid at incorporation. The only mandatory state payments at incorporation are the HK$1,720 incorporation fee and the HK$2,150 first-year Business Registration fee (combined HK$3,870, approximately USD 493). If the Hong Kong joint venture company later capitalizes a Mainland China operating subsidiary, the PRC Company Law registration capital schedule of that subsidiary will apply, but the Hong Kong company itself carries no escrow capital obligation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the Company was incorporated on the day of [date] under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) of the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, with Certificate of Incorporation No. [number] duly issued by the Companies Registry of Hong Kong, and with an issued share capital comprising [number] ordinary shares of HK$1.00 each, subscribed by the shareholders of the People's Republic of China and the joint venture overseas partner; AND WHEREAS the Company is registered with the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department of Hong Kong under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), and it is destined to operate a fast-casual self-serve Chinese Malatang broth bowl restaurant franchise in Hong Kong for which statutory food business licensing, fire safety certification and environmental clearances are mandatory. NOW THEREFORE IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. CORPORATE INCORPORATION ACKNOWLEDGMENT. The incorporation of the Company, the adoption of its Articles of Association, the appointment of the initial subscribers, and the registration of the Company as a private limited company be and are hereby fully acknowledged, ratified, confirmed and accepted by the Board in all respects, and the Directors are instructed to cause the Certificate of Incorporation and the Business Registration Certificate to be framed and displayed at the registered office as required by law. 2. SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUE OF SHARE CAPITAL. The allotment and issue of the subscribed ordinary shares of HK$1.00 each to the shareholders as recorded in the Statement of Capital and the Return of Allotment of the Company be and are hereby confirmed, ratified and approved; and the Directors be and are hereby empowered, with full discretion, to receive payment of the subscription monies, to issue share certificates under the common seal (if adopted) of the Company, and to register the corresponding entries in the Register of Members in accordance with the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) and the Articles of Association. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Directors be and are hereby authorized, jointly and severally, to open, operate, and maintain one or more corporate current, savings, settlement and merchant accounts with licensed banks in Hong Kong for the purposes of the Company; and the following persons, namely [Director A] and [Director B], be and are hereby authorized, any two acting jointly or any one acting with the Company Secretary, to sign, execute, endorse, draw, deposit, transfer and negotiate all cheques, drafts, bills, mandates, remittances and banking instructions on behalf of the Company, including local point-of-sale settlement and royalty wire payment rails. 4. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed and established at [registered office address] in Hong Kong; the statutory records of the Company shall be maintained at such premise, and the responsible Director is hereby directed to notify the Companies Registry and the Business Registration Office of the registered office address through the appropriate prescribed forms. 5. APPOINTMENT AND POWERS OF OFFICERS. [Director A] and [Director B] be and are hereby appointed as the Directors of the Company, each to hold office for an initial term; and [Company Secretary] be and is hereby appointed as the Company Secretary, whose qualifications satisfy section 475 of the Companies Ordinance; such officers are authorized to execute documents, make statutory filings and represent the Company before the Companies Registry and other public authorities. 6. LICENSING AND OPERATIONS AUTHORIZATION. The Directors be and are hereby authorized to apply for and obtain the Food Business Registration under the Food Business Regulation (Cap. 132X), the Fire Services Certificate, building and structural safety consents, environmental clearances, and all other operational permits requisite for the fast-casual self-serve broth bowl business, and to enter into all leases, franchise agreements, equipment supply contracts, and employment arrangements incident thereto. 7. GENERAL POWERS. Any two Directors, or one Director with the Company Secretary, be and are hereby authorized to take every necessary action, execute all instruments, and effectuate all filings, remittances and payments required to give full effect to the foregoing resolutions, and this authority shall remain in full force until expressly revoked by the Board. ADOPTED as the First Board Resolution of the Company on the date first written above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Pre-Incorporation Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry - Cyber Search Centre (e-Search) and Name Screening Unit, Operations Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an exhaustive name search on the Companies Registry public e-Search portal to confirm that the proposed English name and optional Traditional Chinese name are not identical to, or so similar to, an existing company name as to be misleading within the meaning of section 100 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). Prepare not fewer than three ranked names in English and Traditional Chinese, and obtain a signed consent-to-use letter from any third party whose trademark or connected mark appears in the proposed name. The name is screened for prohibited words suggesting government patronage. Submit the search record electronically and retain the printout as part of the incorporation dossier.
required_dossiers: Proposed English and Traditional Chinese company names (three ranked candidates)
Cyber Search Centre name search report printout
Consent-to-use letters for sensitive or trademarked names
Subscriber identity documents (HKID or passport) of all founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is queried or rejected, substitute the next ranked candidate name by withdrawing and resubmitting the application through the e-Registry portal; if rejection is based on similarity, the incorporator may apply in writing to the Registrar of Companies for a direction within 14 days, citing the distinguishing features of the name and the legitimate business interest of the applicant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Form NNC1 and Electronic Incorporation Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry - e-Registry Portal / One-Stop Company Registration and Business Registration e-Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute and deliver Form NNC1 (Incorporation Form - Private Company Limited by Shares) together with the Articles of Association, which must be signed by each subscriber in the presence of a witness. State the registered office address in Hong Kong and provide the particulars of at least one director and a company secretary qualified under section 475 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). Submit the package electronically through the e-Registry portal and settle simultaneously the incorporation fee of HK$1,720 and the first-year Business Registration fee of HK$2,150. Upon successful processing, the Companies Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the integrated system issues the Business Registration Certificate.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Form NNC1
Articles of Association signed by all subscribers and witnessed
Incorporation fee payment receipt (HK$1,720)
Business Registration fee payment receipt (HK$2,150)
Consent-to-act forms from the proposed director and company secretary
Registered office address consent or tenancy document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or requires further particulars, file a written response and any amended forms within 14 days of the request; if registration is refused on name conflict, file a fresh Form NNC1 with an alternative approved name; if the refusal raises a jurisdictional issue, apply under section 112 of the Companies Ordinance for reconsideration with supporting submissions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Business Registration Certificate under the One-Stop Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office (BRO), Inland Revenue Department - integrated with the Companies Registry One-Stop Company Registration Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), the Company must hold a Business Registration Certificate before commencing the restaurant operation. The one-stop incorporation environment automatically issues the Business Registration Certificate contemporaneously with the Certificate of Incorporation. The Company must physically display the certificate at the registered business premise of the Malatang self-serve restaurant, and, if the shop operates under a trading name different from the corporate name, apply for branch registration. Thereafter, the certificate must be renewed annually within 30 days before expiry; non-renewal attracts a surcharge and late filing penalty.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (copy)
Form NNC1 filed records
Tenancy or lease agreement for the restaurant business premises
Identity documents of the designated business operator/manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration Certificate is not issued due to system interruption, attend the BRO in person with the payment proof to obtain an emergency printed certificate; any error in the registered particulars is corrected by filing Form IRBR200, and any overcharged fee is recovered by refund application to the Business Registration Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Governance and Return of Allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry - Operations Branch for statutory filings; Company Board officers for internal statutory books; licensed bank for corporate account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the First Board of Directors meeting and minute the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution. Deliver the Return of Allotment on Form NSC1 to the Companies Registry within eight days of any allotment of shares made after incorporation, with the accompanying statement of capital. Maintain at the registered office the Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Company Secretaries and, where applicable, the Register of Charges as required by the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). Issue share certificates and record them in the share ledger; open the corporate bank account under the banking mandate approved by the Board; deposit the subscribed capital; and affix the common seal, if adopted by the Board.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the First Board of Directors meeting
Form NSC1 Return of Allotment
Share certificates issued to subscribers
Register of Members, Register of Directors and Register of Company Secretaries (Cap. 622 statutory books)
Bank account opening mandate and specimen signatures of authorized signatories
Company common seal certificate, if adopted
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For a late Return of Allotment, pay the prescribed default penalty and apply to the Companies Registry for relief from civil penalty under the relevant provisions of Cap. 622; if the bank rejects the mandate, redraft the banking resolution and re-execute the mandate with full signing authorities within two business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Restaurant Food Business Registration, Fire Safety and Premises Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) - Food Business Registration Unit; Fire Services Department (FSD); Buildings Department (BD); Labour Department Occupational Safety and Health Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prior to the opening of the self-serve Chinese Malatang restaurant, obtain a Food Business Registration Certificate for a 'Restaurant' business under the Food Business Regulation (Cap. 132X) by submitting the prescribed application form, FEHB 89, together with the premises floor plan, tenancy proof, ventilation and air-conditioning drawings, and the effluent drainage layout showing the grease trap installation. Coordinate with the Fire Services Department for the fire safety inspection covering means of escape, emergency lighting, fire alarm and automatic sprinkler coverage, and obtain the Fire Safety Compliance Letter or Certificate of No Objection. Secure Buildings Department approval for the commercial change of use and a structural load assessment for the self-serve counters, storage shelving and kitchen equipment. Upon hiring staff, notify the Labour Department and procure Employees' Compensation insurance.
required_dossiers: FEHB 89 Application for Food Business Registration
Premises floor plan with kitchen and dining layout
Tenancy agreement or certificate of ownership
Ventilation and grease trap design drawings
Fire Services inspection report and FSD approval letter
Buildings Department compliance certificate for change of use
Structural engineer report on floor loading
Environmental Protection Department waste and effluent declarations
Employees' Compensation insurance policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If FEHD queries or suspends the food business application, rectify the cited deficiencies, such as installing anti-scorch guards on self-serve burners or upgrading the grease interceptor, and resubmit with amended plans for re-inspection; if the Fire Services Certificate is deferred, engage a Registered Fire Service Installation Contractor to remediate the installations and resubmit within 30 days; any refusal of a food business licence may be appealed to the Food Appeal Board under the Food Business Regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) - Food Business Registration under Cap. 132X; Fire Services Department (FSD) - Fire Safety Compliance; Buildings Department (BD) - Premises Use Approval; Environmental Protection Department (EPD) - Environmental Compliance; Labour Department - Workplace Safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Registration Certificate for 'Restaurant' Premises under the Food Business Regulation (Cap. 132X), covering the fast-casual self-serve Chinese Malatang broth bowl outlet with open kitchen cooking stations and self-service buffet counters.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department (EPD) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Environmental Compliance Division, Waste Management and Water Policy Branch
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration (Category III) - No Full EIA Report Required: the fast-casual restaurant premises are not a designated project under Schedule 2 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499) unless located within a sensitive conservation area; a written EIA exemption/registration confirmation is obtained for the commercial premises, and the operation is instead governed by the Water Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 358), the Waste Disposal Ordinance (Cap. 354) and the Air Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 311).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Kitchen and dishwashing wastewater must pass through a grease interceptor of not less than 3,000 litres effective capacity or a 10-minute retention time at peak flow before discharge to the foul sewer, and must not exceed the effluent standards of the Technical Memorandum on Effluent Standards under the Water Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 358), namely pH 6.0-9.0, Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD5) 500 mg/L, Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) 700 mg/L and Total Suspended Solids (TSS) 500 mg/L; where discharge loadings exceed the sewerage authority thresholds, a Trade Effluent Discharge Licence or trade effluent surcharge arrangement must be secured from the Drainage Services Department. Kitchen fume exhaust must be ducted to a roof-level discharge with electrostatic precipitators and activated charcoal filtration achieving not less than 85% removal of grease and particulate matter, compliant with the Air Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 311) emission limits on odours and volatile organic compounds; any chemical waste from cleaning agents must be stored in labelled compliant containers and collected only by an EPD-licensed chemical waste collector.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Services Department (FSD) Fire Safety Certification or Certificate of Compliance must be obtained under the Fire Services Ordinance (Cap. 95), including automatic sprinkler coverage where the restaurant floor area exceeds the statutory threshold, a fire alarm system, emergency lighting, exit signage, and a fire load assessment for the open-burner self-serve Malatang stations; Buildings Department (BD) approval is required for change of use, structural load certification for kitchen and buffet equipment, and a certified evacuation route plan; Civil Defence preparedness requires an Emergency Action Plan with trained fire wardens; the Labour Department Occupational Safety and Health Branch clearance requires a workplace risk assessment, electrical equipment isolation protocol for self-serve warmers, slip-resistance treatment for broth-spill zones, and Employees' Compensation insurance confirmation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, exercising the state tax, VAT, invoice and export-rebate jurisdiction over mainland China; the operative online access is the nationwide Unified E-Tax Bureau (electronic tax service platform) through the provincial STA e-tax portals. Hong Kong SAR's Inland Revenue Department remains a separate territorial tax administration but is not the registration authority for this PRC-established Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Form the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture under the PRC Foreign Investment Law by obtaining the required foreign investor filing from the local Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), which issues a Foreign-Invested Enterprise Business License bearing an 18-character Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). 2. Treat the USCC as the statutory Tax Identification Number; no separate mainland China TIN certificate is issued to the enterprise for corporate income tax or VAT. 3. Within 30 calendar days of business license issuance, complete the initial tax registration through the Unified E-Tax Bureau using the USCC; the STA opens the taxpayer file and registers the JV's tax categories, including CIT, VAT, urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, stamp duty and related items. 4. If the JV applies for or becomes a VAT general taxpayer, the USCC is the VAT registration number and the JV is enrolled in the STA digital e-invoice system. 5. For the Hong Kong non-resident shareholder/licensor without a PRC permanent establishment, the JV as payer and withholding agent satisfies withholding registration and remittance obligations on dividends, interest, royalties or service fees; the Hong Kong parent is not issued a mainland China VAT ID for passive investment income. Where the PRC e-tax system requires a system-generated non-resident taxpayer identifier for treaty relief, that identifier is created through the foreign-payment withholding module, not as a PRC VAT registration number; the Hong Kong shareholder should obtain a Hong Kong tax-resident certificate only for the purposes of a claim under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement. 6. If the Hong Kong shareholder operates through an actual PRC permanent establishment beyond passive equity investment, it must complete a separate non-resident enterprise tax registration through the same e-tax route and obtain its own non-resident taxpayer registration file; the JV's USCC is separate and will not cover that PE. 7. After tax registration, complete China Customs exporter registration and trade foreign-exchange payer/receiver filing, because export VAT zero-rating and export-rebate eligibility require the USCC, customs business file and foreign-exchange business file to be aligned.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None, as to entity classification. PRC law does not provide a check-the-box or flow-through election for a limited-liability Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture; the JV is taxable at entity level as a PRC resident enterprise. The only relevant election in the indirect-tax layer is the VAT small-scale taxpayer simplified method at a 3% collection rate while annual taxable sales remain below the mandatory general taxpayer threshold; crossing CNY 5,000,000 of annual taxable sales triggers compulsory general VAT taxpayer registration. Hybrid mismatch positions are handled under statutory anti-avoidance and controlled foreign corporation rules, not elective elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For the restaurant/catering service business the headline VAT rate is 6% for general taxpayers and the simplified collection rate is 3% for small-scale taxpayers, subject to the STA's temporary reduced 1% small-scale taxpayer policy where applicable. There is no turnover exemption from basic tax registration for incorporated enterprises; the JV must complete tax registration within 30 days of business license issuance. The mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration threshold is annual taxable sales above CNY 5,000,000; below that threshold the JV may remain a small-scale VAT taxpayer, and small-scale taxpayers with monthly taxable sales at or below CNY 100,000 (quarterly CNY 300,000) are eligible for the temporary zero-VAT ordinary-invoice exemption while that policy is in force. Packaged retail goods sold off-premises and central-kitchen wholesale supplies may be classified under the 13% goods VAT rate, requiring careful revenue-classification analysis.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The JV must issue Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoices through the Unified E-Tax Bureau digital invoice module for B2B and B2C domestic sales and for export sales. Each digital invoice carries a unique invoice code, encrypted information and anti-counterfeit QR code and is transmitted in real time to the STA invoice management database; no private offline invoice is legally usable for VAT input credit or export rebate. VAT Special Invoices supporting input tax credits are validated against the STA invoice service system before the customer may deduct input VAT. There is no separate municipal fiscal stamping mechanism for mainland China VAT; tax clearance is effected through the real-time e-invoice upload and reconciliation of sales and export records in the e-tax database. Export goods are separately cleared through China Customs electronic customs systems, and customs clearance data are matched with the STA export-rebate module.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A VAT general taxpayer may claim 0% VAT and input-tax refund on goods that are legally exported from mainland China under a customs export declaration and for which the JV is the seller of record, the goods physically leave Chinese customs territory, the sale is made

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for mainland China operations; the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as the currency board authority for the HKD and the Linked Exchange Rate System for the Hong Kong treasury side.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Hong Kong SAR operates as a fully convertible, offshore-style currency jurisdiction under the Linked Exchange Rate System administered by the HKMA; the Hong Kong dollar trades freely and there are no cap or current account conversion restrictions. The mainland China component of this Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is subject to a uniquely bifurcated FX regime: current account transactions such as trade, royalties, and service fees are generally convertible once the underlying transaction is verified and supported by invoices and contracts, while capital account movements such as equity injection, shareholder loans, and return of investment require specific SAFE registrations and step-by-step approval. Under the current account convertibility framework, the JV may pay cross-border royalties or supplier invoices in foreign currency after tax authorities confirm withholding; however, profit remittance to the Hong Kong parent remains a highly scrutinized matter requiring audited financial statements, a verified underlying profitability position, and a valid foreign exchange payment application submitted through a domestic designated bank. All export proceeds generated by the Chinese production and supply side must be repatriated through a domestic settlement account; SAFE performs monitoring but does not impose a mandatory conversion ratio. The principal remittance hurdles are tax clearance certification, proof of the underlying economic substance, and consistency between the JV articles of association and the actual beneficial ownership structure, with stricter documentary scrutiny when the Hong Kong conduit is viewed as a passive treasury vehicle rather than an operating commercial partner.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For goods export receivables, the statutory repatriation window is generally 180 days from the date of export customs declaration unless an extension is granted by SAFE with documented commercial justification; the mandatory conversion ratio is zero because SAFE abolished compulsory surrender and now requires export receipts to be credited to a designated foreign exchange account or settled into RMB on a voluntary basis, subject to trade monitoring and reconciliation with customs declarations, VAT records, and logistics documents.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (CNY and Multi-Currency)
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for mainland China because foreign fintech EMIs and neobanks are not licensed by the PBOC or SAFE to maintain domestic corporate accounts, execute RMB/CAP settlement, or perform statutory FX verification for a Chinese JV; they cannot substitute for a Tier-1 domestic bank. For the Hong Kong treasury and licensing side, a Hong Kong-licensed Stored Value Facility or Money Service Operator may support ancillary merchant collections and small-value remittance, but it remains legally and practically constrained from acting as the primary cross-border banking bridge for equity injection, royalty remittance, or trade settlement. Overall viability rating: Low for the mainland entity, Moderate only for auxiliary HK treasury functions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mainland Chinese banks generally mandate physical appearance by the legal representative and at least one statutory director before a branch compliance officer for initial corporate account opening, in addition to certification of the company chop and board signatory specimens; remote consular proxy opening is rarely permitted, and notarized powers of attorney are accepted only under strict bank-by-bank KYC discretion. The Hong Kong parent may be onboarded under HKMA-observed corporate KYC using remote identity verification if the bank has a mature digital onboarding framework and the directors produce original passports plus commercial registry documents; otherwise a board resolution and notarized power of attorney in favor of an in-branch director are required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity arising from holding layers spanning mainland China and Hong Kong SAR, with the JV possibly being treated as a conduit for undisclosed parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current certified Certificate of Incorporation for the JV and Hong Kong parent, complete share register, ultimate beneficial ownership declaration, board resolution naming all authorised signatories, notarised passports and residential proof for every 25% or greater shareholder, and a documented source-of-funds narrative for the original equity contribution, accompanied by bank statements supporting the historical capital trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive self-serve restaurant POS deposits across the franchise network appearing as structured small-amount transactions or unverified sales diversion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Daily POS and restaurant management system settlement reports, terminal identification and merchant licensing records, sales tax declarations with matching VAT invoices, franchise royalty schedules, bank statements showing stable store-level cash cycles, an internal AML procedures manual, and periodic independent audit reports covering cash handling, inventory, and revenue reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border royalty and franchise fee wire flows to Hong Kong tripping bank filters for intellectual property valuation, treaty shopping, and tax leakage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered trademark and franchise IP assignment agreements, arm's length royalty valuation report, license fee calculation workbook with store count and revenue assumptions, signed franchise agreements with all licensed outlets, double tax treaty relief application or withholding tax certificates, and evidence of substantive management activity at the Hong Kong parent such as board minutes, employee records, and payment of local expenses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential mismatch between the declared USD or HKD equity investment and the actual CNY working capital usage in the Chinese operating entity, raising concerns of round-tripping or disguised lending.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE Foreign Direct Investment registration confirmation, capital verification report issued by a licensed CPA, publication or statutory notice of capital contribution, bank capital settlement receipts, board-approved cash flow projection linking injected capital to restaurant build-out, equipment purchases, working capital needs, and payroll, plus executed lease agreements and vendor contracts supporting the planned deployment of funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For inbound equity injection, the Hong Kong parent should remit via SWIFT MT103 from a Hong Kong corporate bank account to the JV's domestic designated capital account under the SAFE Foreign Direct Investment registration. The remittance must use the approved FX purpose code associated with direct investment equity injection, and each incoming tranche must be matched with the returned foreign exchange business registration certificate issued by the local SAFE branch. The receiving designated Chinese bank will convert the proceeds into CNY upon presentation of the board resolution, joint venture contract, and capital verification statement; after conversion, a licensed CPA issues the final capital verification report, and funds remain restricted to the business purposes stated in the JV's articles, business license, and approved capital contribution plan.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operating disbursements for raw materials, packaging, and franchise supplies should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 for cross-border vendor payments using current account service or goods purpose codes, or through commercial letters of credit and documentary collections for bulk trade settlements where supply-chain documents are required. Franchise royalty and management fee outflows to the Hong Kong licensor must be paid by MT103 based on the approved franchise contract, with the bank required to verify the invoice, withholding tax payment certificate, and the current-account royalty remittance form. Local fast-casual store receivables are settled through domestic POS and QR clearing in CNY, pooled into a consolidated operational account, and periodically used for working capital; the pooled CNY funds are then clearly segregated from cross-border payment facilities to avoid mixing store-level cash flow with foreign exchange settlements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Bank-executed deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts in USD/HKD/CNY aligned to the JV's genuine trade and capital payment exposure, with maturity matching the underlying invoice or royalty schedule.

Onshore CNY foreign exchange swaps and cross-currency swaps permitted by SAFE for real current account or capital account hedges, subject to bank counterparty limits and a documented underlying exposure.
Offshore USD/HKD forward contracts through the Hong Kong treasury company for centralised management of the combined JV and parent group exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards restricted to offshore RMB positions booked by the Hong Kong treasury entity, while the onshore Chinese JV is expected to use deliverable forwards and swaps with designated domestic banks.

Speculative option layers, leveraged derivatives, and naked currency positions are strictly prohibited; all FX hedging instruments must be supported by verified transaction exposure, board-approved hedging policy, and client suitability documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form NAR1) under Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fees escalate with delay: over 42 days up to 3 months HKD 1,200; 3-6 months HKD 2,400; 6-9 months HKD 3,600; 9-12 months HKD 4,800; over 12 months risks court prosecution with fines up to HKD 50,000. Persistent failure to file annual returns when the Registrar reasonably believes the company is not carrying on business triggers administrative strike-off under Cap. 622 s.746(2), publication in the Gazette, and dissolution unless restoration is obtained.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate renewal under Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the certificate expiry date; the renewal payment must be made within the month immediately preceding the expiry date shown on the current Business Registration Certificate.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Carrying on business without a valid Business Registration Certificate is an offence; a maximum fine of HKD 50,000 and imprisonment for up to one year may be imposed. The IRD may institute collection proceedings for the unpaid renewal fee and impose surcharges; sustained non-renewal is treated as evidence of no active business and can reinforce a Companies Registry strike-off assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (Form BIR51) accompanied by audited financial statements and tax computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month from the date of issue of the return; for a standard 31 December accounting year-end the return is typically issued in April and is due by 1 May of the following tax year, subject to extension arrangements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-filing without reasonable excuse exposes the company and its directors to fines up to HKD 10,000 for the first offence and HKD 20,000 for subsequent offences, plus treble undercharged tax under Inland Revenue Ordinance Cap. 112 s.80(2). The IRD may issue estimated assessments, add 5% and 10% late-payment surcharges, and pursue collection through distress and court proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (Form IR56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the form is issued by the IRD, normally on or before 1 May immediately following the tax year of assessment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An employer who fails to furnish IR56B without reasonable excuse is liable to a maximum fine of HKD 10,000 per offence; continued default may lead to higher fines, estimated assessments, and exclusion of payroll deductions in the company's Profits Tax Return.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Hong Kong imposes no revenue, total-asset, or headcount threshold that exempts an active non-dormant limited company from statutory audit. The mandatory trigger is qualitative: every non-exempt company incorporated under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) must appoint a Certified Public Accountant (practising) as auditor and must file audited financial statements with its Profits Tax Return. The only statutory exemption is for a dormant company that has passed the prescribed special resolution and remains free of significant accounting transactions; once the company resumes business, hires staff, or holds statutory assets, the audit duty revives. The audit must be conducted in accordance with Hong Kong Standards on Auditing issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must comply with the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) Part 9 and be prepared under Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) or, where the entity is an eligible private company, the HKFRS for Private Companies issued by the Hong Kong Institute of CPAs. The statutory auditor's report must be addressed to the members and accompany the financial statements when submitted to the Inland Revenue Department.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not operate a separate annual UBO filing. The annual confirmation of ownership is embedded in the NAR1 Annual Return, which must list all members and disclose shareholdings as at the anniversary date. Under the Companies (Amendment) Ordinance 2018, each company must maintain a Significant Controllers Register covering individuals or entities holding 25% or more of shares or voting rights, or with significant control; any change must be entered in the register within 7 days of the company becoming aware. Share transfer instruments must be processed in the Register of Members promptly, and if the company refuses to register a transfer, written notice of refusal must be given within 2 months. The Significant Controllers Register is not a public registry, but it must be kept on-site and be made available to law enforcement and government officials on demand.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Company Secretary
Register of Charges and copies of instruments creating charges
Minute Books of members' meetings and board meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - USD 1,800 per annum for registered office plus corporate secretarial services; USD 300 - USD 700 for registered-office address only.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 8,000 per annum for a single-entity fast-casual self-serve food franchise with HKFRS audit and tax computation; group consolidation or revenue complexity above HKD 50 million will increase the fee.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (mainland China Enterprise Income Tax); Hong Kong profits tax at 16.5% for corporations, reduced to 8.25% on the first HKD 2,000,000 of assessable profits under the two-tiered regime
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small and low-profit enterprise preferential rate of 5% for annual taxable income up to RMB 3 million; additional 100% super deduction for eligible R&D expenses; potential 15% preferential rate for qualifying advanced technology or encouraged industry enterprises in specific regions; Hong Kong territorial-source exemption for offshore profits and concessionary 8.25% rate on first HKD 2,000,000 profits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: China: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (A类) Form, Form A01041, filed via the electronic tax bureau platform (电子税务局); Hong Kong: Profits Tax Return Form BIR51 filed via eTax/eTAX portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (China EIT with quarterly provisional filing; Hong Kong Profits Tax annual)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: China: Annual EIT return due within 5 months after the close of the fiscal year (May 31), with quarterly provisional returns due within 15 days after each quarter-end; Hong Kong: Profits Tax return generally due within 1 month of the issue date of the BIR51 notice, extendable by the IRD upon application

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating revenue / gross receipts from catering and franchise operations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross sales of self-serve broth bowl stores and master franchise royalties. For non-resident JV shareholders, this line is the starting point for attributable profits; ensure intercompany transactions with the Hong Kong parent are recorded at arm's length and reconcile with the Local File

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, including food ingredients, labor, and store supplies
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only costs supported by compliant VAT special invoices from mainland suppliers. Cross-border procurement from the Hong Kong JV entity must be tested for transfer pricing; denied deductions trigger a 25% EIT catch-up and potential deemed dividend WHT at 10%

Verify that management fees or brand royalty charges from the Hong Kong entity are consistent with the arm's length royalty rate benchmark embedded in the transfer pricing documentation. An excessive royalty is a classic base-erosion red flag generating a deemed distribution to the non-resident

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: selling, general, administrative, and financing expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to non-resident shareholders is subject to 10% WHT and thin-capitalization limits (1:1 debt-equity ratio). Deductibility requires the loan to be actually funded, not merely automated equity; otherwise recharacterized as an equity dividend

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income before non-taxable income, tax-exempt income, and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entry guidance: taxable income must exclude treaty-protected business profits unless the Hong Kong entity creates a permanent establishment in mainland China. A Chinese-Malatang franchise with self-serve stores and local staff almost always creates a fixed place of business PE, subjecting the attributable profit to 25% EIT; the Hong Kong profits tax territorial-source rules may then provide unilateral credit only if mainland tax is actually paid

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss offset, non-taxable income, tax exemption, and adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Utilize the 5-year carryforward cap strictly. Losses of the mainland JV are not transferable to the Hong Kong parent; the Hong Kong parent cannot group relief Chinese losses. Intercompany loss absorption devices (e.g., excessive service fees) are ignored and trigger fraud penalties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apportionment of foreign-tax credits, preferential tax rates, and foreign income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the JV derives Hong Kong-source income, credit against mainland EIT is limited to the mainland tax otherwise payable. For outbound dividends to the Hong Kong shareholder, use treaty rate certificate to reduce WHT from 10% to 5% only after filing the Non-resident Taxpayer Application for Treaty Benefits and submitting the Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final computed tax payable, prepaid provisional tax, and balance due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border profit repatriation is not a deduction to the JV. Dividends are distributed from after-tax surplus. The 10% withholding (reduced to 5% under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA on dividends if qualified beneficial owner is a Hong Kong enterprise) is declared on the withholding return within 15 days of the payment date

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: China: late filing surcharge of 0.05% per day on unpaid amount, administrative fine between RMB 2,000 and RMB 10,000; intentional underreporting or false declaration causing tax underpayment invites 50% to 5x fine and criminal tax evasion liability over RMB 100,000. Hong Kong: late filing penalties up to HKD 10,000; additional daily penalty of HKD 500 assessed by the District Court where delinquency persists; knowing and willful evasion can attract a fine of HKD 10,000 per count plus imprisonment for 6 months escalating to 12 months for tax fraud

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% non-resident dividend withholding tax under China, reduced to 5% for a Hong Kong beneficial owner who is the registered shareholder of at least 25% of the mainland JV's capital under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA (Article 10)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The JV must withhold the statutory 10% before remittance. To claim the 5% treaty rate, the Hong Kong shareholder must (i) obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the IRD for the relevant year; (ii) file the《非居民企业享受税收协定待遇办理报告表》/ Non-Resident Enterprise Treaty Benefits Application Report with the mainland tax authority, usually ahead of the dividend resolution; (iii) supply a beneficial ownership declaration and substantiation that no intermediary individual holds title; (iv) prove the substantive business and bank accounts in Hong Kong; and (v) present audited accounts and a legal-person status certificate stamped by the Hong Kong Registrar of Companies. Filing is made via the electronic tax bureau with a mandatory beneficial owner self-assessment form; if the IRD/State Taxation Administration considers the Hong Kong entity a conduit or lacking economic substance, the 10% domestic rate is restored, plus interest and late penalties

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 10% WHT; treaty rate reduced to 7% under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA for industrial/commercial/cultural royalties; interest: statutory 10% WHT; treaty rate 7% (Article 11), with 0% possible for financial institutions under specific conditions. Both require prior treaty-benefit filing and demonstrate arm's-length royalty rates and genuine financing, not profit shifting

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: China: Local File required where the total related-party transactions amount exceeds RMB 100 million (annual); Master File and Country-by-Country report required at RMB 1 billion consolidated revenue threshold; Hong Kong: record-keeping and contemporaneous documentation required where controlled transactions exceed HKD 10 million (or HKD 30 million per individual transaction type)
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Sino-French JV's business in mainland China carries substantial economic substance in the form of physical Malatang stores, local Chinese employees, food supply chain, and on-site management. Franchise royalties paid to Hong Kong are benchmarked under the TNMM; the Hong Kong treasury entity must have its own deal-making activity, staff, decision-making, and risk control to be recognized as a beneficial owner. Hong Kong Corporate ESR does not apply to a pure trading/holding vehicle unless it carries protected activities, but the mainland tax authority applies China's General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR, Article 48 of the EIT Law) and the OECD Principal-Purpose Test under the MLI to deny treaty benefits to shell companies. Ongoing, genuine business purpose, board minutes, real decision-making, and payroll in Hong Kong are required to support CIGA

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing EIT returns and withholding returns that understate gross sales, inflate cross-border franchise royalty deductions, omit mainland store revenue, or shift 80% of JV income to the Hong Kong affiliate through artificial service fees without economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: China EIT Law Article 63 and Tax Collection Administration Law Articles 63-64: monetary penalty of 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax, daily late-fee of 0.05% on the underpayment, and potential criminal prosecution under Article 201 of the Criminal Law for tax evasion exceeding RMB 100,000 with a 10% false-declaration ratio resulting in imprisonment of up to 7 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally orchestrate false invoicing or cross-border profit shifting are jointly and severally liable for the enterprise's unpaid taxes, interest, and penalties where the tax obligation arises from intentional concealment; civil asset restitution orders freeze personal accounts; travel bans (出境限制) imposed by the tax authority continue until full payment; criminal arrests for tax evasion lead to imprisonment of the controlling director and the company's monetary fine in parallel

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell / Treaty Abuse and Dividend Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Hong Kong JV as a letterbox entity with no employees, no office, no decision-making over the Chinese franchise business, solely to claim the 5% DWT treaty rate on outbound dividends or to receive interest/royalties without substantive economic ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: China GAAR (EIT Law Article 47, Implementation Regulations Article 120) permits the tax authority to disregard the Hong Kong vehicle and recharacterize the payment as a taxable dividend at 10% or as taxable income of the ultimate resident; anti-abuse provisions push the rate up to mainland 25% plus late penalties; State Taxation Administration may deny DTA benefits under the Principal-Purpose Test; Hong Kong Inland Revenue Ordinance Section 61A counteracts tax avoidance and imposes additional 100% assessable tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing the treaty-benefit self-declarations face personal fraud liability under the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court when lying in the TRC or beneficial ownership certificates; civil recovery to repay treaty-avoided withholding plus triple administrative fine; the individual is blacklisted by the customs/tax exit-control mechanism, banned from board membership in mainland entities, and criminally liable for fraudulent invoicing under Criminal Law Article 205A with imprisonment from 6 months to 7 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Corruption and Cross-Border Profit Transfer
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Funneling franchise royalty and store profits through shell treasury companies, using unregistered overseas bank accounts, accepting cash under the counter at Malatang stores to avoid corporate EIT, or paying bribes to local licensing officials to obtain or renew the statutory food-operating license
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law: administrative penalty of RMB 2 million to RMB 10 million for banks or enterprises knowingly involved, and freezing of all illicit proceeds; Commercial and food-license fraud leads to revocation of NationalFood Business License (食品经营许可证) and a lifelong industry ban for the responsible legal representative; the State Administration for Market Regulation imposes a fine of 10 to 30 times the illegal business proceeds; criminal conviction under Criminal Law Article 176 for illegal deposits or Article 164/389 for commercial bribery carries confiscation and imprisonment up to 15 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil is pierced because the JV is used as an instrumentality of fraud; the controlling director's personal assets are subject to civil attachment orders in Chinese courts; travel ban and exit control issued by the public security border authorities; the director personally is fined and imprisoned for 5 to 10 years for bribery of government licensing officials, and lifetime disqualification as a company director is imposed by the State Administration for Market Regulation
